title.narrative: Baseline Development for the Revitalized FRIEND-Nile Initiative

description.narrative:
Initiated in 1997, FRIEND-Nile became an integral component of UNESCO’s global FRIEND-Water program, specifically addressing water-related challenges across the Nile River Basin. Spanning all Nile Basin Countries, it includes the Arab Republic of Egypt, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Eritrea, Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Republic of Kenya, Republic of Burundi, Republic of South Sudan, Republic of the Sudan, Republic of Uganda, and United Republic of Tanzania. FRIEND-Nile facilitates cooperative research and dialogue to enhance the region's water security through shared knowledge, collaborative management strategies, and integrated scientific frameworks. The Nile Basin faces profound water-related challenges amplified by population growth, economic pressures, climate change, political tensions, and transboundary governance complexities. Given this context, FRIEND-Nile acts as a unique and neutral science-driven platform that bridges scientific inquiry and practical policymaking.
In March 2025, UNESCO IHP organized a Regional Workshop on Capacity Gaps, Priorities and Pathways Forward for the UNESCO-IHP FRIEND-Nile Initiative. With the outcomes of the inclusive consultative process involving experts from all Nile Basin countries, a revitalized FRIEND-Nile Strategy was formulated. The revised strategy works towards three expected results: enhancing hydroclimatic data collection and sharing, increasing understanding of the impacts of global change on hydrological regimes and their extremes and deepening understanding of water-society interactions in transboundary basins. During the workshop the participants highlighted the need for strengthening data sharing, climate adaptation, capacity building, and governance improvements while leveraging science diplomacy and regional collaboration.
The proposed small-scale activity (SSA) will serve as a de facto inception phase for the revised FRIEND-Nile initiative. In the past, Flanders has already supported this initiative through two previous phases, leading to valuable scientific collaborations and achievements. This activity aims to develop the baseline for the renewed FRIEND-NILE programme development. The SSA will also identify gaps in information as well as available datasets, and integrate these in IHP-WINS, UNESCO’s data-sharing and visualization platform that adheres to the principles of Open Science. The proposed SAA will also implement a workshop with all Nile basin countries to develop a bankable project proposal, to ensure the continuity of the FRIEND-Nile initiative.
To enhance capacity for climate adaptation, the SSA will also provide the baseline and enabling environment for the development of regional CRIDA case studies during the envisioned full project phase. CRIDA, Climate Risk Informed Decision Analysis, is a methodology developed by UNESCO and partners to identify potential water security risks in a region or watershed, caused by climate change and other drivers, by providing a step-wise planning process to identify and address the challenges for sustainable water resources management. Additionally, the SSA will contribute to promoting science diplomacy and regional collaboration, which are particularly relevant in the Nile Basin.
